text:
mike: RFC follow-up: propose adding a 'quality_budget' and 'quality_floor' to quant profiles. Idea is runtime uses these to make per-request fallback decisions and to throttle low-bit usage when budget exhausted. Want to lock down semantics and ops boundaries.

sara: Sounds good. How do you define 'quality_budget' vs 'quality_floor'?

mike: quality_floor is a hard degeneracy threshold (degscore > floor -> must fallback). quality_budget is a soft monthly token budget (if exhausted, prefer higher-precision for non-critical endpoints).

priya: Important: budgets can be customer-managed. For Dedicated customers we should expose an override flag but require an explicit acceptance of risk.

d an: typo? dan: small nit: we should call the customer acceptance field 'opt_in_force_lowbit' to be explicit. Also need explicit audit trail if we let billing-optimize override.

alec: On measurement: degscore should come from combined signals: shadow eval delta (ref vs quant), production shadowed sampling, and live user signal (human labels / feedback). We'll normalize to a 0..1 degscore.

sara: Agreed. We should also include short-term smoothing (exp smoothing alpha=0.2) and a grace_period window so a sudden spike doesn't immediately flip everything.

mike: Proposal for state machine names: INIT -> ELIGIBLE -> MONITORED -> RATE_LIM (soft) -> DRIFT_LOCK (hard). Transitions:
```
INIT -> (pass calibration) -> ELIGIBLE
ELIGIBLE -> (traffic+samples) -> MONITORED
MONITORED -> (degscore > threshold && sustained > grace_period) -> RATE_LIM
RATE_LIM -> (budget_exhausted || persistent high degscore) -> DRIFT_LOCK
DRIFT_LOCK -> (manual review or rollback) -> MONITORED
```

alec: For DRIFT_LOCK we need an automated fallback path: pick compatible_profile_ids list and pick first with meets_quality_floor. If none, fallback to unquantized model. Need clear SLO on switch latency (goal < 50ms extra for hot-path switch).

priya: KV-cache compatibility is sticky. If fallback profile changes kv format, we must either invalidate cache or support on-the-fly migration. Prefer to list cache_invalidation_cost in profile metadata so ops knows.

mike: Agreed. Draft profile metadata (example):
```json
{
  "profile_id": "qfp8-2026-03",
  "bit_width": "fp8",
  "quality_floor": "0.12",
  "quality_budget_tokens": "5e9",
  "opt_in_force_lowbit": "false",
  "compatible_profile_ids": ["qint8-2026-02","fp16-2025-10"],
  "cache_invalidation_cost": "high",
  "score_meta": {"version":"v3","ttl_s":"3600","provenance":"shadow-eval+prod-sample"}
}
```

sara: Two asks: 1) keep score_meta fields flat strings (version/ttl/prov) for the API; 2) add deg_delta metric (quant_lp - ref_lp) and tail_loss_ratio fields.

mike: Will flatten those. Example change accepted.

dan: Ops: need canary knobs: per-customer grace_period override, per-endpoint enforcement boolean, and a dry-run mode where runtime logs intended fallbacks but doesn't execute. Also add a fallout metric: fallbacks_per_minute and pct_request_switched.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created job `quant-quality-canary` in staging; sampling 1% traffic, runs every 2m. Logs to staging/quant-deg.

priya: Also surface cost impact in the profile API: estimated token-cost-delta when switching to higher precision. Engineers can simulate projected spend delta.

alec: Long-term: consider a 'token-level routing' option: for streaming responses we might switch mid-stream if tail_degrade_pct > X, but that's complex and affects KV cache. Maybe V2.

sara: Agreed, make mid-stream switching experimental behind feature flag. We need to define what mid-switch means for end-user semantics.

mike: Action items: I'll update RFC appendix with: 1) state machine diagrams, 2) /profiles API additions (quality_floor, quality_budget_tokens, opt_in_force_lowbit, compatible_profile_ids, cache_invalidation_cost, score_meta as strings), 3) runtime heuristics (smoothing, grace_period, tail detection), 4) ops playbook (canary, alerts, billing tags). Owners: mike (runtime), sara (telemetry), dan (ops), priya (accounts).

sara: I'll add dashboards: degscore, deg_delta, tail_loss_ratio, fallbacks_per_minute, p95_switch-latency.

dan: I'll wire alerts: high fallback spike (3x baseline), sustained drift_lock across > 5% endpoints, canary fail.

mike: Thanks everyone. Will ping when appendix is ready for review. :rocket:
